about: Every part and asset, and how finished it is (docs/assets.md section 10). Only the owner sets approved.

assets.note: Casks on a rack, tapped.
Baskets of apples and turnips, one lidded.
The church's strongbox: the bank.
The god itself; not exported yet.
The town's second creature.
A hollow hooded soul tapering to a wisp, arms as trailing sheets; drifts, can't be killed.

The walker (picked from shade variant C), polished: human-sized hooded soul leaning under a lumpy dark bundle with two iron bands and shoulder straps; a recessed glowing face with eye strokes; a crook in the right hand, the left fist on the strap; the player's gear poking out (sword hilt, pickaxe, round shield, a boot on a lace) and keys at the hip; wisp for legs. 1428 tris, 5 colours.
Shade variant A (owner to pick): a footsoldier in a kettle hat holding a broken spear, unravelling into ribbons below the waist.
Shade variant D (owner to pick): a tall veiled mourner, robe trailing on the water, a crown of soul-flame candles on the head.

The shades (picked from variant B), polished: the high hunched arch kept; a shaped mask (frowning brow, cheek planes, slanted void eye slits and a long void mouth, wrapping back over the skull) instead of the oval with a slot; torn soul-cloth sleeves hanging from the arms; the trail now tapers, sways and lifts at the tip. 2564 tris, 3 colours.
Stooped hooded traveller with a staff and a soul lantern; waits at the end of the long way.
Dry grey reeds from a dark tussock, some snapped over.
A leaning drowned timber, split top, iron band.
Four pale arms clawing out of a dark patch, about a tile; the hazard that holds you.
Others' dropped gear: a pack, a half-sunk shield, a boot.
Tall bone-pale leaning stone, wet dark foot.
Shorter, broader bone-pale leaning stone.
A spiked barricade to drag across the road.
The ringing chamber's ropes and sallies.
An arched recess in a wall with stacked bones and skulls
Spare boards and a lid leaning on a wall
A pot on a chain from three poles over a fire ring.
Rake, pitchfork, scythe leaning together
Fish split and hung to dry.
Bunches drying from a beam
Hides drying on a frame.
A ladder leaning on a wall.
The cask in Sour Hollow the vitriol mites gather round: split, salt-crusted, the ground dead round it.
A flat stone over one of the drowned.
A market stall or two for the square.
A stall of cloth in bolts and folded lengths.
A stall of fish in shallow crates.
Millstones leaning against a wall.
Nets hung to dry on poles
The square's notice board.
Reeds cut for thatch, stooked and stacked.
A log half sawn through on a sawhorse.
A pole gate lying in the verge by the old toll-house.
The wardens' spears and shields.
The dead-house's bier, where every player first wakes; a shroud over it.
Rough boards along its length, wider at the shoulders; open and lid variants
A shop or clerk's counter.
A clerk's writing desk with an open ledger.
Shelves of crockery over cupboards
Shelves of jars.
A lectern with a ledger on it.
A clothes press.
A body laid out under a shroud, on a bier
A base, a body and a moulded top
Built from the pieces it drops as.
Tolling's landmark on its knoll: stone, three storeys, an open belfry with the bell; seen across the basin.
A stone porch over the head of a stair down: the cellar kit's outdoor entrance
The twin of Tolling's bell in a belfry standing out of the lake, its roof fallen in on one side (The Bell's end).
Widdermill: a wheel-house and an undershot wheel that turns in the game. The wheel-house and race on the mill's river side; the mill itself is the village kit, as data. The wheel is WaterMillWheel.
The mill's undershot wheel alone, its origin on the axle, so the game can turn it.
The wardens' gate on the road: a timber gatehouse or barred gate. Two log towers and a covered walk over the road; the gate is WaygateGates.
The waygate's two leaves, shut and barred.
The first test prop (172 triangles); not exported yet.
Iron cage with a pale soul flame on a leaning drowned post; restores blood.
The soul lantern used: flame gone, a dim cinder in the cage.
Four candles and a burnt-out stub run together in a small pool of their wax; cold soul flames.
A dozen candles of every height, the outer ones leaning, on a low mound of melted wax.
A landmark: a great melted heap of wax about a tile across with dozens of candles, tall at the top, some gone out.
Three small wax rafts with one or two candles each, drifting on the water (surface at the origin).
An iron pricket stand, three feet, a drip dish and a candle
A street lantern on a timber post
One tile of interlocking iron links between two posts.
A fount for tiers 1-3 (object monument_fount): a round drum basin, blood standing below its lip, five bronze fangs standing up round it.
A fount for tiers 4-6: a basin on a stem with a bronze band, six fangs.
A fount for tiers 7-10: a broad eight-sided basin on a chamfered block, eight fangs.
Its depleted state: the blood brimming dark, the fangs closed over it.
Tier 1 (Religion 1). A wayside needle on one step, two founts: the frontier tier. Laid on the tile grid: layout() gives its founts, their stand tiles and its blocked tiles.
Tier 10 (Religion 90). The needle and four lesser needles on a terrace raised over a court of eight founts. Laid on the tile grid: layout() gives its founts, their stand tiles and its blocked tiles.
Tier 2 (Religion 10). Two steps, a bronze band on the needle, three founts. Laid on the tile grid: layout() gives its founts, their stand tiles and its blocked tiles.
Tier 3 (Religion 20). Taller, four founts at the corners. Laid on the tile grid: layout() gives its founts, their stand tiles and its blocked tiles.
Tier 4 (Religion 30). Three steps, a merlon collar on the needle, corner pinnacles, four founts. Laid on the tile grid: layout() gives its founts, their stand tiles and its blocked tiles.
Tier 5 (Religion 40). A niched pedestal under the needle (a reliquary's place), four founts. Laid on the tile grid: layout() gives its founts, their stand tiles and its blocked tiles.
Tier 6 (Religion 50). An octagonal plinth, four lesser needles, six founts. Laid on the tile grid: layout() gives its founts, their stand tiles and its blocked tiles.
Tier 7 (Religion 60). A broad octagon, four steps, runnels from the founts to the needle, six founts. Laid on the tile grid: layout() gives its founts, their stand tiles and its blocked tiles.

Tier 8 (Religion 70). A tall niched pedestal under the needle, four lesser needles at the corners, eight founts. Laid on the tile grid: layout() gives its founts, their stand tiles and its blocked tiles.
Tier 9 (Religion 80). A cross-shaped plinth, a lesser needle at each arm's end, founts paired on the arms. Laid on the tile grid: layout() gives its founts, their stand tiles and its blocked tiles.
A monument not yet raised: the plot staked, the first course laid.
The faith's banner on a pole, no cross.
A middle reliquary: an iron-bound casket.
A high reliquary: a silver house-shrine, red glass, a bone showing.
Where a reliquary is placed before a monument.
A low-tier reliquary: wood bound in copper.
One tile of blood runnel, laid end to end.
A proclamation stele with the oath cut in it.
The churchyard's roofed gate.
A cellar trapdoor, shut (object trapdoor_down).
The same thrown open, the ladder's top showing.
A cottage's vegetable rows.
Crops in rows (only flax exists).
A crop strip before the ears turn.
Dry ground cover for the gravel edge.
The open land's scree; parts/rockwork/common/RockScree is the caves'. One may do for both.
A smith's anvil on a block, on its own
A scarred bench with a mortar, a rack of vials and a ledger (object apothecary_bench)
A turf-covered mound, smoking at its vents (object charcoal_kiln)
A smith's open hearth of firebrick under a hood, leather bellows, the anvil beside it (object forge)
A squat clay furnace with a bellows at its foot (object furnace)
A floor loom (Tailoring's weaving).
The lye vat (a station).

Wenna's skinning rack (a station).
The apothecary's still.
The tanner's pit of bark liquor (Tailoring's tanning).
A joiner's workbench (Artifice).
An orchard apple with red fruit; a Foraging node, AppleTreePicked its spent state.
A wind-bent thorn on the dry rise.
The churchyard yew, darker than anything else in the basin.
A clinker rowing boat for the mere and the lake.
Drawn up on the shore and turned over.
One tile of the causeway: two worn slabs a hand above the water.
Two leaning bone-pale stones under a lintel with one soul-mark; the start of the route, about 2 tiles wide.
A single worn stone standing out of the water.
A tile of walkway over the fen, laid end to end.
Where Palmerway crosses the river: stone, one or two arches, cart-wide.
The dry-stone field wall (was WallSpan).
A broken field wall span, half buried in the gravel.
The palisade running from the waygate to water or rough ground.
A shop sign on an iron bracket, in a wall tile's frame Hung out over the street on an iron arm, end-on to the wall, its mark on both faces.
An iron wall sconce with a candle, in a wall tile's frame
A sign hanging from a bracket on a wall tile. A name board fixed flat over the door, lettering painted on.
The caves' boulder; assets/rocks/common/Boulders is the open land's.
The caves' scree; assets/rocks/common/Scree is the open land's. One may do for both.
Coursed stone either side of a built cave doorway.
A timber sluice gate for the millpond and leat.
